title: Re-allocating Vector/Buffer Inside a Tight Loop
pattern: Creating and growing a vector, buffer, or collection inside the body of a repetitive loop.
why_bad: It triggers costly malloc/free operations and potential heap reallocations on every iteration, introducing significant execution overhead compared to reusing existing capacity.
detection: Collection construction (`Vec::new()`, `String::new()`, `vec![]`) located directly inside a `for`, `while`, or loop construct where the collection is discarded at the end of the iteration.
counterexample: The vector must escape the loop or is moved/transferred to another thread. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Allocate a single vector with capacity outside the loop, clearing its elements at the start of each iteration using `.clear()`.
